2607.12739.title: Epistemic Stance Flexibility Probing: Measuring Prompt-Conditioned Register Shift in Large Language Models
2607.12739.paper_summary: A language model may be asked either what experts believe about a contested claim or what it believes about the claim itself. A trustworthy conversational agent should distinguish these two requests and respond in different epistemic registers: neutral attribution in the first case and stance expression in the second. Whether such a shift occurs-and whether it occurs coherently-is not directly assessed by existing benchmarks for accuracy, instruction following, or safety. We introduce ESFP, a behavioral benchmark that treats the contrast between externally attributed and self-attributed prompts as the fundamental unit of measurement. ESFP consists of 104 carefully controlled items spanning six epistemic categories and five phrasing templates, and evaluates model responses along four complementary dimensions: lexical self-attribution, representation-level responsiveness to role framing, sentence-level stance content density assessed by an LLM judge panel, and cross-condition stance consistency. Evaluating eight frontier models from five vendors, we find that epistemic flexibility is largely orthogonal to general model capability: a 27B open-weight model matches the strongest proprietary systems, the flagship model of one family underperforms its lightweight counterpart, and reasoning-optimized models do not consistently exhibit higher flexibility. Stance content density provides the strongest signal, while surface-level lexical markers such as 'I think' can change substantially without corresponding changes in expressed stance. We provide item-level bootstrap confidence intervals, weight-sensitivity analyses, and an explicit discussion of the interpretation limits of the composite score. ESFP measures a model's propensity to adapt its epistemic stance under changing attribution conditions, rather than a general competence measure.
2607.12739.paper_summary_zh: 一個語言模型可能會被詢問專家對於一個有爭議的主張的看法，或是它自己對該主張的看法。<lb/>一個值得信賴的對話代理應該區分這兩種請求，並在不同的認識論範疇中作出回應：在第一種情況下採取中立歸因，而在第二種情況下表達立場。<lb/>這種轉變是否發生，以及是否以連貫的方式發生，並未受到現有準則在準確性、指令遵循或安全性方面的直接評估。<lb/>我們介紹了ESFP，一個行為基準，將外部歸因和自我歸因提示之間的對比視為基本的測量單位。<lb/>ESFP由104個精心控制的項目組成，涵蓋六個認識論類別和五個措辭模板，並沿著四個互補的維度評估模型回應：詞彙自我歸因、對角色框架的表現層級反應、由LLM評審小組評估的句子層級立場內容密度，以及跨條件立場一致性。<lb/>在評估來自五個供應商的八個前沿模型時，我們發現認識論靈活性在很大程度上與一般模型能力是正交的：一個27B的開放權重模型與最強的專有系統相匹配，而一個家族的旗艦模型表現不如其輕量級對應物，並且經過推理優化的模型並不總是顯示出更高的靈活性。<lb/>立場內容密度提供了最強的信號，而像「我認為」這樣的表面詞彙標記可以在表達立場的變化中顯著改變，而不會伴隨著相應的立場變化。<lb/>我們提供了項目級的自助信心區間、權重敏感性分析，以及對綜合得分解釋限制的明確討論。<lb/>ESFP測量模型在變化的歸因條件下調整其認識論立場的傾向，而不是一般能力的測量。
